description:
verification-architecture.md's own Purity Boundary Map classifies the NEW module `~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/registry-path.mjs` (exporting `CITIZENS_REGISTRY_PATH` and `COORDINATOR_HOME`) as 'Pure Core (new, two constants)' -- but this classification directly contradicts the SAME document's own treatment of the underlying primitives these two constants are built from, two rows apart in the SAME table:

(1) `CITIZENS_REGISTRY_PATH` is defined as `path.join(resolveStateDir({env, home}), 'citizens.json')` -- and `resolveStateDir` is explicitly classified, in the immediately-adjacent row of this same table, as '**Effectful Shell** (existing, reused unmodified -- new to this feature, resolves FIND-901) | `~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/state-path.js::resolveStateDir({env, home})` | EFFECTFUL (existing, reused unmodified)'. A constant built by calling a function this same document calls EFFECTFUL cannot simultaneously be 'Pure Core' by this document's own stated convention.

(2) `COORDINATOR_HOME` is defined as 'computed EXACTLY ONCE, at module-load time, via Node's `os.homedir()`' -- `os.homedir()` is a real OS-level read of ambient host/environment state (on most platforms it reads `$HOME`/the passwd database), not a deterministic computation over its own inputs; it is exactly the kind of 'hidden global/environment state' dependency a purity boundary exists to isolate into the effectful shell, not fold into the pure core.

This is not merely academic: this spec's OWN Verification Strategy assigns proof tiers based on this exact Pure-vs-Effectful distinction (Tier 0/1 = no runtime execution / no I/O; Tier 2/3 = real filesystem/env-dependent). Labeling `registry-path.mjs` 'Pure Core' invites a Phase 3 implementer or reviewer to treat `CITIZENS_REGISTRY_PATH`/`COORDINATOR_HOME` as testable with a zero-I/O, no-environment-control Tier-1 unit test -- but genuinely proving either constant's correctness (e.g. that COORDINATOR_HOME really does resolve `/Users/anicca` on this host, or that CITIZENS_REGISTRY_PATH really does route through resolveStateDir rather than a stale/cached value) requires controlling the real process environment/`os.homedir()`, i.e. genuinely effectful-shell-style Tier-2 testing -- exactly the kind of testing PROP-403e/PROP-403f (correctly) already specify for THIS SAME module's other properties. The mislabeling creates a live risk that this ONE row's own proof obligation (PROP-105k, PROP-103d, PROP-403f) gets under-scrutinized at Phase 3 specifically because the Purity Boundary Map tells a reviewer 'this is pure, nothing to check for hidden environment coupling here' -- precisely the failure mode the adversary's own purity_boundary check exists to catch.

New, resolves FIND-701 (critical): this SAME module ALSO exports `COORDINATOR_HOME` ... computed EXACTLY ONCE at module-load time via Node's `os.homedir()`
